about: The time dial. Each map names its Library of Congress picture, matched places (xy in full-resolution sheet pixels, lonlat on the real earth) and the lettering on it (spine through the letters, h their height). generator/dial_tools.py build fits a stiff bend through the matched places, writes the bent sheets to static/dial/ and fills in drawn, frame, mid and at. early holds the stops before any sheet can be laid on the earth. off: true keeps a map on record but off the dial.

early.head: A people, not yet a place
early.says: William of Rubruck rides from the Black Sea to the Mongol court at Karakorum and back, and writes of the Tartars as a people on the move, with their tents, carts and herds. The line is his road. On the world maps of his century in this atlas, the word is not yet lettered as a country.

early.head: The great wall maps do not know the name
early.says: The largest medieval world map to survive was drawn while the first reports from the Mongol courts were already in Europe, yet it carries none of them. Its northern Asia is still Scythia, with Gog and Magog walled in by Alexander. It is a round picture of the world with east at the top, so it cannot be laid on the real earth. Open it to see.

early.head: The word reaches the maps
early.says: One of the earliest maps to letter Tartaria as a region, with a note explaining it and little pictures of Tartar wagon camps, and with Gog and Magog set close by. It is engraved on a round metal plate with south at the top, so it cannot be laid on the real earth either. Open it to see.

maps.head: Three Tartarys around the Caspian
maps.title: [Carta marina navigatoria Portugallen navigationes ...] sheet 3; the running head over this sheet reads: ...IS TEMPORIBUS RECOGNITOS ET AB ANTIQUORUM TRADITIONE DIFFERENTES
maps.title_plain: Sea chart of the Portuguese voyages and of the whole known world, sheet 3 of 12: Russia, the Black Sea, the Caspian, Persia and the steppe
maps.says: This sheet letters TARTARIA three times. The largest stands on the steppe north of the Caspian Sea, over the tent of the khan, and two more east of the Caspian are tied to older country names: TARTARIA CORASINE (Khwarezm) and TARTARIA TORQVESTEN (Turkestan). North of the Sea of Azov the plain is called CAMPESTRIA TARTAR, and note after note across the sheet says that Russians, Armenians and Persians live under the Tartars.
doubts: The heading TERRA MONGAL ET QUE VERA TARTARIA DICITUR is not on this sheet. Every strip of sheet 3 was searched on close views; the heading must stand on the neighbouring sheet to the east (sheet 4), which is a different picture.

The sheet can be laid on the earth honestly in its western two thirds: the Black Sea, the Levant coast, Russia and the west and north of the Caspian come from sea charts and reports and fit to within a few hundred km. On the shared sheet it sits turned about 40 degrees, which is only the projection at this far western longitude, not a fault.

East of the Caspian there is not one place that can be matched (no Samarkand, Bukhara or Urgench on this sheet; the country there is drawn from Ptolemy with rivers and old province names). The eastern third, where TARTARIA CORASINE and TARTARIA TORQVESTEN stand, is therefore carried along by the western fit and its position on the earth is only a rough guide.

The Caspian is drawn as an oval lying east to west, as on the old sea charts, so its true north-south shape cannot be matched; the points on it (Volga delta, Kura mouth, Ural mouth, south shore) pull against each other.

Derbent could not be found by name on the west shore of the Caspian. Astrakhan is lettered only as agitarcam in the list of names at the Volga delta, with no sign of its own. CASANA (Kazan) is lettered as a country near the Don, with no town sign, and was not used.
Sarai is read from the town lettered Sala ciuit. on the Volga; the river name dayr fl. is read as the Yaik (Ural); Grassan is read as Kashan. All three are marked not sure.
CAMPESTRIA TARTAR: the second line reads TAR TAR and seems cut short (for Tartarorum or Tartarie).
A small name east of the Sea of Azov reads Tacaria over Tarmacho (about x 2190, y 2985). It may be a slip for Tartaria but it is lettered with a c, so it is not recorded as a Tartary label.

Many of the written notes on the sheet name the Tartars (sub mandato Tartarorum, sub dominio Tartarorum, sub tributo tartarorum, the boxed note beginning Tartari semper morantur in campis). These are text blocks and are not recorded as labels.
The title given is the running head printed over this sheet; the map's main title stands on another sheet.

maps.head: One word, letter by letter, across the steppe
maps.title: RVSSIAE, MOSCOVIAE ET TARTARIAE DESCRIPTIO. Auctore Antonio Ienkensono Anglo, edita Londini Anno 1562 & dedicata illustriss. D. Henrico Sydneo Wallie presidi.
maps.title_plain: A description of Russia, Muscovy and Tartary, by Anthony Jenkinson, Englishman, published at London in 1562 and dedicated to Sir Henry Sidney, Lord President of Wales
maps.says: The word TARTARIA is lettered once, in big letters spread one by one across the open steppe from the Don and lower Volga eastward past the Yaik toward the country above Tashkent. It is not divided into parts; smaller names such as Nagaia, Cassacki, Turkmen and Kirges sit inside and around it, and the far north is given to the Samoyeds instead. A note beside Samarkand calls that city the former capital of all Tartary.
doubts: This is a 1914 black and white Russian reproduction that follows Ortelius's 1570 reduced plate, not the 1562 London sheet; fine lettering is blurred in places.

The word also appears inside two text notes (Samarkand 'olim totius Tartariae metropolis' and Little Khorasan taken 'adiuvantibus Tartaris 1558') and in the title; these are text blocks and are not recorded as labels.

The also names CASSACKI and TVRKMEN are broken over three and two lines and are given one entry per line. BOGHAR, SHAMARGHAN, KIRGES, TASKENT, MHOGOL, COLMACK, BAIDA and MOLGOMZAIA are also lettered as region names but left out to keep to eight entries.
The Vardo and Kola spots are read from a dark, crowded coast and may be 20 to 30 pixels off.
The Ob, Sibir, Tashkent and Kashgar came from hearsay and sit far from their true places; the Caspian is drawn wider east to west than north to south, so its shore towns fit badly.

maps.sheet: Tartary, or the kingdom of the Great Khan
maps.head: The Great Khan's whole realm under one word
maps.title: TARTARIAE SIVE MAGNI CHAMI REGNI typus
maps.title_plain: Map of Tartary, or the kingdom of the Great Khan
maps.says: Ortelius letters TARTARIA once, in large capitals across the steppe north-east of the Caspian, and adds in small script that it takes in Asiatic Sarmatia and both Scythias of the ancient writers. He does not divide it into Great, Little or Chinese Tartary; the rest of the country is filled with the names of hordes and with Marco Polo's kingdoms such as Tangut, Camul, Tenduc and Cathay, all of them, by the title and the note in the lower cartouche, under the Great Khan.
doubts: The word Tartary also occurs inside blocks of text, which were not recorded as labels: the title cartouche (TARTARIAE SIVE MAGNI CHAMI REGNI typus), the lower left cartouche ('Continet hec tabula oem Tartariam'), the note by the Great Khan's tent ('lingua Tartarorum') and the Altai note ('oes Tartarie imperatores').
A town on the China coast is lettered Tartaho (about 3550,3730); it is a town name, not the word Tartary, and was not recorded.

The interior east of Samarkand and the whole north-east coast (Scythicum prom., Tabin, Arsareth, the Strait of Anian) are legend, so nothing fixes the sheet there; the fit rests on the Black Sea, Caspian, the Russian north coast to the Ob, the China coast and Japan.
No fitting place could be found in the south-west and south (Persia and India are covered by a cartouche and blank lettering), so that side of the sheet is held only by Tabriz, Merv and Termez.
Moscow and Bukhara are not on this sheet (it begins east of Moscow and uses Gastaldi's names beyond the Caspian), and Canton lies off the bottom edge; Korea and Novaya Zemlya are not drawn.
The Caspian is drawn as an east to west oval and Hangzhou (Quinsai) far north of Ningbo, so those places land far off however the sheet is laid; they are true identities and were kept.
Merv, Termez and Margilan are read from Gastaldi-style names (Maru, Terment, Merglan) and marked not sure.
The stub's 'Siberia' pin at 105E 61N was changed to the town of Sibir near Tobolsk, which is what the symbol stands for.

maps.head: The name reaches the Arctic sea
maps.title: ASIA with the Islands adioyning described, the atire of the people, & Townes of importance, all of them newly augmented by I: S: Ano. Dom: 1626
maps.title_plain: Asia with the adjoining islands described, with the dress of the people and the towns of importance, all newly enlarged by John Speed, 1626
maps.says: Speed letters TARTARIA in large spaced capitals across the country between the Volga and the Ob, running up from north of the Caspian Sea. The word comes back three more times: as a tribe (Kaski Tartari) in the steppe below it, as a town called Tartar in the empty far north-east, and on the water as The Tartarian Sea along the whole Arctic coast. A note beside the Great Wall says it was built against sudden inroads of the Tartars, and one of the costume figures in the border is labelled Tartarian.
doubts: The tribe name under TARTARIA has a meridian line through its third letter; it is read here as 'Kaski Tartari' (long s, probably the Kazakhs), which earlier notes gave as 'Kalbi Tartari'. 'Kalki' is also possible.

The note on the Great Wall ('...against the suddaine in fall of ye Tartars on this side', about x 4350-4720, y 2040-2090) and the border figure lettered TARTARIAN (lower right) hold the word but are a text note and border decoration, so they are not recorded as labels.
North-east Asia is drawn by guess (Mongul, Tenduc, Tartar, a coast running to a strait with America), so nothing fixes the fit there beyond Beijing and northern Japan.
The Caspian is the old east-west oval, and Samarkand is set far east; both are kept as true places the mapmaker misplaced.
The picture is a photograph of an open book with a gutter near x 3600 and some page curve, and the plate edge is slightly out of square (corners near 619,476; 6630,451; 6644,5120; 649,5148).

maps.sheet: Great Tartary, the Mogul empire, Japan and China
maps.head: Great Tartary, from the Ob to the Pacific
maps.title: MAGNÆ TARTARIÆ, MAGNI MOGOLIS IMPERII, IAPONIÆ et CHINÆ, Nova Descriptio
maps.title_plain: A new description of Great Tartary, the Empire of the Great Mogul, Japan and China
maps.says: The words TARTARIA MAGNA, Great Tartary, are spread one letter at a time across the whole of inner Asia, from the river Ob to the Pacific coast and from the Arctic shore down to the Great Wall of China. Inside that space the sheet names many separate peoples and kingdoms, among them the Kazakh Tartars, Chagatai, Turkestan, the Mongols, Cathay and Tangut, and the Arctic sea above is called the Tartar Sea. Siberia is only a small name by the Ob, and the far north-east is filled with names from Marco Polo and from legend, such as Magog and a town and river called Tartar.
doubts: Three short Latin notes on the map body also use the word and are not recorded as labels: 'Castrum contra irruptionem Tartarorum' near 6800,3045, 'eunt ac redeunt Tartari' near 3400,3280, and 'Regnum Tartariae Sepulchra sunt' near 5600,3240, besides the note on the trumpeters near 6700,2330.
'Tart.' after ZACATAY is cut short on the sheet, so it may mean Tartaria or Tartari.

North of China and east of the Ob almost nothing on the sheet is real: the Arctic and north-east coasts are guesses, there is no Baikal, Aral or Amur, and the towns come from Marco Polo. The fit there rests on the Ob and Yenisei mouths and on the Dutch survey of Yezo and Sakhalin at the east edge, so the place of the TARTARIA lettering on the earth is loose.
The Volga mouth and Astrakhan fall off the left edge, so the west side is held by the Ural river mouth, Samara, Saratov and Bolgar.
Tashkent is lettered far to the east of Samarkand and is kept out of the fit.
Two places stay flagged after a second look because the sheet itself is wrong there: Verkhoturye (about 1000 km off) and the south-east corner of the Caspian (about 500 km off).

maps.says: This small sheet writes Tartary only twice. Western Tartary is the pink country between the Caspian and the Gobi, holding Turkestan, Bucharia, the Dzungars and Kashgar, with Tibet coloured as part of the same block. Chinese Tartary is the green country of the Mongols and Manchus north of China, while everything Russian is called Siberia and split into Tobolsk, Yakutsk and other governments with no Tartary name at all.
doubts: The scan is small (2601 by 3271), so town rings can only be placed to about 5 pixels, which is 40 km or so on the ground.

Only two Tartary names are on the sheet, each set on two lines: WESTERN over TARTARY, and CHINESE (north of the Amur) with TARTARY far to the south of it. No Russian, Independent or Eastern Tartary is lettered.
Tibet and Little Tibet share the pink colour of Western Tartary, so the colour block is wider than the name strictly says.
Arabia and the Red Sea fit worst (Mecca and Bab el Mandeb are 500 to 600 km off when left out): the sheet draws the Red Sea too far west and sets Mecca deep inland.
The Arctic coast from Novaya Zemlya to the Lena is loosely drawn; the Gulf of Ob, Taimyr and Lena mouth spots are approximate.
Okhotsk has no town symbol and the head of Penzhina Bay is unnamed; both are read from the coast shape.
The also list is capped at eight; Bucharia, Calmucs, Great Turky, Buratians, Tungusi and the Russian governments of Astrachan, Orenburg and Irkutsk are also lettered in this country.
The spines for the YAKUTSK and TOBOLSK government names are approximate, as their letters are widely spread among other lettering.

maps.says: By 1849 the word Tartary has shrunk to one modest line of spaced capitals in central Asia, running from just west of the Sea of Aral across Khokan to the edge of Soongaria, with no border or colour of its own. It is threaded among the names that have taken its place: Turcomania, Khiva, Great Bucharia, Khokan, Kirguis and Turkestan. Farther east the sheet letters Soongaria, Mongolia, Little Bucharia, Mandshuria and Chinese Empire with no Chinese Tartary at all, and the only other survival is the small Channel of Tartary between Saghalin and the mainland.

maps.head: The country is gone; a people and a gulf keep the word
maps.title: JOHNSON'S ASIA BY JOHNSON AND WARD.
maps.title_plain: Johnson's Asia, by Johnson and Ward (no imprint line is lettered on the sheet; plate number 82 in the corner)
maps.says: On this American family atlas sheet of 1862 the country called Tartary is gone. Where older maps spread that name, this one letters TOORKISTAN with Khiva, Bokhara and Khokand, and Siberia, Outer and Inner Mongolia and Manchooria, all inside the Russian Empire and the Chinese Empire. The word survives in only two small places: KIRGHIZ TARTARS, the name of a people on the steppe north of the Aral Sea, and the Gulf of Tartary, the water between Saghalin and the mainland.
doubts: Search for the Tartar word: the whole map body inside the neat line was read on close views in overlapping strips about 660 sheet pixels wide (x 290 to 4610, y 190 to 3600), row by row from the Arctic coast to the bottom edge, with a second closer look at the Kirghiz steppe, Toorkistan, Mongolia, Manchooria, the Amoor and Saghalin. Only two letterings hold the word: KIRGHIZ TARTARS (two lines, a people) and Gulf of Tartary (a water). Nothing else turned up: no Tartary, Chinese Tartary, Independent Tartary or Crim Tartary anywhere, on land or sea. One small patch of open Pacific near the right edge (x 4310 to 4610, y 3120 to 3280) was seen only on the reduced check picture; it holds no lettering.

The names that stand where Tartary used to be, confirmed on close views: TOORKISTAN in large capitals, with KHIVA, BOKHARA and KHOKAND in smaller spaced capitals inside it and TOORKOMANIA beside the Caspian; SIBERIA and RUSSIAN EMPIRE in long arcs; OUTER MONGOLIA, INNER MONGOLIA, MANCHOORIA, CHINESE EMPIRE and BOD OR TIBET. The eight largest are in 'also'; the three khanates and the Siberian provinces (TOBOLSK, TOMSK, IENISEISK, IRKOUTSK, IAKOUTSK, OKHOTSK) are smaller and left out.

The last A of SIBERIA is taken as the capital A at about (3727, 684), among the letters of the province name OKHOTSK; the letters of SIBERIA, RUSSIAN EMPIRE, IAKOUTSK and OKHOTSK cross each other in east Siberia, so the east end of the SIBERIA outline is the least certain of the outlines.

No imprint or copyright line is lettered on this sheet; the title block reads JOHNSON'S ASIA BY JOHNSON AND WARD and the corner carries the plate number 82. The place and date (New York, 1862) come from the library record, not from the sheet.

Fit: 80 places, north of about 5 degrees north, reaching all four sides. Most land within 100 km. The poorest are at the edges: East Cape and North East Cape on the Arctic rim, the north tip of Nova Zembla, the Kolyma mouth, and Aden in the south-west corner; Lake Balkhash and Khokand are simply misplaced by the mapmaker. All were re-read on close views and kept.
The sheet runs south to about 5 degrees south (Sumatra, Borneo, New Guinea); no places were matched south of Ceylon, so the bend is not held there.

Kirghiz Tartars lettering is very small (capitals about 13 sheet pixels high) and Gulf of Tartary is small italic (about 22); both outlines were checked against the lettering on cut pieces of the check picture.

maps.head: Only the water remembers
maps.title: ASIEN.
maps.says: The word Tartary is gone from the land on this German atlas map. The only trace is a small name in the water between the mainland and Sakhalin, Tatar'scher Golf, the Tartar Gulf. Where older maps wrote Tartary, this one writes Russisches Reich and Chinesisches Reich in big spaced letters, with West-Sibirien, Ost-Sibirien, Turkestan, Ost-Turkestan, Mongolei and Mandschurei beneath them.
doubts: Maker and date: the sheet itself carries 'Verlag R. Grossmann, Berlin S.W. 29.' under the lower right corner, 'Red. O. Brunckow, Berlin.' under the lower left, 'Alle Rechte vorbehalten.' twice, and page numbers 50. and 51. at the top corners. No year is printed anywhere on the sheet. The 1894 date rests on the Library of Congress catalogue entry for the atlas, not on the sheet. The content agrees with a date around then: the colour key has 'Deutsche Schutzherrschaft', Kaiser Wilhelms Land is on New Guinea, Burma is in the British colour, Wladiwostok is lettered, and no Siberian railway is drawn.

Title as lettered in the block at the lower left: 'ASIEN.' with 'Maßstab 1:30 000.000.' beneath it. The small inset is headed 'Völkerkarte von ASIEN. Auf Grundlage v. Friedr. Müller's "Allgem. Ethnographie" nach v. Haardt, Gerland u. A.'

Search for the Tartar word: the whole map body was read on close views, in sixteen overlapping pieces from x 1400 to 6025 and y 300 to 3800 (four rows of four, each about 1250 by 950 sheet pixels), then three pieces down the west side (x 290 to 1540, Europe, the Mediterranean and north-east Africa with the title block), three along the south edge (y 3750 to 4350), the top and bottom margins, and tighter views of the Volga and Crimea, the Kirgisen-Steppe and Turkestan, East Turkestan, Mongolia, Manchuria, the Amur and Sakhalin. The only lettering found with the word is 'Tatar'scher Golf' beside Sakhalin. Nothing else turned up: no Tartarei, Tatarei or Tataren on land anywhere, including the Crimea, the Volga and Kazan country, and the steppe.

The ethnographic inset (x 390 to 1810, y 3140 to 4180) and its key were read on close views. Its key lists Papua's & Melanesier, Afrik. Neger, Australier, Arktiker & Hyperboreer, Malayen & Polynesier, Dravida's, Mongolen (mit einsilb. Spr., mit mehrsilb. Spr.) and Mittelländer (Basken, Kaukasier, Hamito-Semiten, Indo-Europäer). There is no Tataren in the key or on the inset. The inset's own land names are West-Sibirien, Ost-Sibirien, Turkestan, Ost-Turkestan, Mongolei, Mandschurei, Tibet, China, Iran, Arabien, Hindustan and so on.
'Tatar'scher Golf' is small italic lettering crossed by a meridian line and crowded by 'Constantinowsk'. The ending before Golf reads as r (Tatar'scher) but could be n.

Names that took Tartary's place: the eight in 'also' are the largest. RUSSISCHES REICH and CHINESISCHES REICH are each set on two lines, so each has two entries. Also lettered across the same country but left out of the eight: 'Kirgisen-Steppe' north of the Aral Sea and Lake Balkhash, TIBET, 'Gobi-Wüste (Schamo)', Buchara and Chiwa.

Fit: places are kept north of about 8 degrees north. A fold runs down the middle of the sheet near x 3120 and the two halves do not meet perfectly there. The worst places when left out are at the far corners (East Cape at Bering Strait, Aden, Manila, the Arctic capes), where the sheet's projection curves most and there are no neighbours beyond to hold the fit. Arkhangelsk, Obdorsk, Fu-san, the south tip of Kyushu and Manila were placed from the coast beside the name because no clear town ring could be made out.
